status: Shared seed helper paths mapped; root constructor caller remains unidentified
summary: Reviewed the 15:26Z Seed-B uploads and continued static analysis. The latest runtime seed/address pair is 5B4AE67D9C2A8F61 / 0001BF0004E84EFD. Fresh caller extraction ties the session to NMS.exe SHA-256 671de22649274b49fa07f5a246bc7252c4e08bb9ab623d2e65722fbab4e497a4; its caller window matches the live exact-root bytes. Disassembly of the hash-matched uploaded caller windows narrows the flow: function candidate 006388A0 reads the descriptor primary seed at object+0x138 (descriptor at +0x128) and use_seed at +0x140. Calls at 006377B6 and 00637D86 pass an object through as the second argument. In the 00637660 wrapper path, an incoming stack argument is forwarded through helper 00637DB0 and initializer 006377E0, which copies/initializes the embedded descriptor at +0x128 via call 00227A40. This is direct byte/argument-flow evidence that seed source is supplied upstream of 00637660; it is not evidence of how that value was generated. The available windows do not include callers or vtable slots for 00637660, so the universe-address-to-root-seed derivation remains unproven. A read-only static reference scanner is now committed on this lane at agent-patches/seed-lineage/seed_b_trace_static_callers.py (commit 6243812f4e7b94c75f0d6055055c2fdd947e7f76; SHA-256 7fa2dca6a6ab02caec5601b9549cf1d352da78dbc4539cb12d3c2e12255f4d20). It was syntax-checked and tested against a synthetic PE fixture for both a direct rel32 call and an absolute pointer slot. The scan's 325-byte windows place each reference exactly at offset 160, so they omit the preceding function setup and do not show enough of the caller to identify source-object initialization. The matching NMS.exe is not present in the shared workspace. Existing lane tooling can extract bounded RVA windows locally without launching NMS. An additional offline export around the three caller sites is now the only blocker; no game traversal, probe restart, or controller capture is required. User attached NMS(1).exe, which is byte-identified by SHA-256 671de22649274b49fa07f5a246bc7252c4e08bb9ab623d2e65722fbab4e497a4. I parsed its PE .pdata function table and disassembled full caller/helper ranges. Measured flow: incoming R9 to 00637660 is passed unchanged to 00637DB0, preserved as R14, then passed as the first stack argument to 006377E0; 006377E0 forwards it to 00227A40, which copies/initializes the embedded descriptor at destination object+0x128. The three direct callers supply local records at [rbp-0x20], [rbp-0x28], and [rbp-0x38]. This locates the descriptor source argument but does not link these static paths to the live root event or establish a universe-address-to-seed transform. Continued offline analysis of the supplied matching executable. The object-creation path carries the 00637660 incoming R9 descriptor through 00637DB0/006377E0 and copies it at 00227A40; the generated-object consumer path at 006388A0 falls through into adjacent .pdata code at 006388F9, which reads object+0x138 and tests +0x140. One direct caller, 001B2CF9, fills that descriptor field through an invertible 64-bit mixer of a sign-extended 32-bit global state value. Inverting the mixer for the three known root-seed candidates gives no sign-extended 32-bit input, so this path cannot directly emit those candidates if the observed copy path is unchanged. The other two callers (02D042E1, 02D04AF8) remain under investigation. Added exact .pdata caller bounds to the scanner; 2/2 focused tests and py_compile passed. No new game run or traversal is needed while the static trace continues. Additional offline trace of the two remaining callsites in the hash-matched NMS.exe found that both enter a shared helper at 02D03EE0. Callsite 02D042E1 belongs to .pdata range 02D0400B..02D0455C; it builds its local descriptor seed field from a context value plus an iteration value, then applies the observed multiply/xor mixer. Callsite 02D04AF8 belongs to .pdata range 02D04690..02D04F47; its enclosing function is called from 02D053A0..02D05DC0, and that caller itself also calls the same shared helper at 02D05ACE. Static setup at 02D03D41 passes its context pointer from [rbp+0x148] and an integer from [rbp+0x150] into that helper. This narrows the two paths to shared generated-resource/context processing; none of the stack or pointer values are available statically, and no path has been shown to be the live root-resource descriptor. This is still not proof of a universe-address-to-root-seed derivation. A further PE unwind-chain check now links the 02D042E1 runtime fragment back to 02D03EE0..02D0400B and links the live root AddResource fragment at 00638DF0 back to 006388A0..006388F9, independently corroborating the prior 006388A0 entry candidate. The latest uploaded capture ties root seed 5B4AE67D9C2A8F61 to external walk caller 02C0497A within 1.782 ms, but that is a generic indirect callback and is not one of the three direct 00637660 constructor callsites. It therefore does not identify which constructor path initialized the root descriptor. The static scanner now reports PE unwind-chain parents; 3/3 focused tests and py_compile pass. Root seed derivation remains unproven. Reviewed newer shared batch research-uploads/20261004T205413Z-all-saved-evidence-4ad05293 on main (commit 370d1a7eff808fba4a4b16202cd9b3e003e4b098). The 20:53:18Z root event is fresh (probe 0.3.35) and again pairs address 0001BF0004E84EFD with root seed 5B4AE67D9C2A8F61, use_seed=true, AddResource return 00638DF5, descriptor 000001192EBECD28. owner+0x10 remains zero/null. Its exact caller remains generic external virtual callback return 02C0497A, not a static 00637660 constructor caller. The uploaded upstream/seed-analysis exports have the same manifest SHA-256 values as the previous batch, so they add no changed static trace. Continue lane-owned work by identifying direct callers of 006388A0 and whether one can be associated with the descriptor/root event; no traversal requested. Additional offline caller trace: 006388A0 has a second wrapper path at 00637C40 (separate from 00637660). The 00637C40 path preserves incoming R9 into 00637DB0, then invokes 006388A0 with its generated object. Its only two direct callers are both in parent routine 016866EC..01686993 at 016867A4 and 01686912. Those sites pass two different local descriptors ([rsp+0x68] and [rbp-0x58]) and store returned objects in separate parent-owned slots. This establishes a second descriptor-producing path and narrows the static search, but does not tie that parent or either descriptor to the live root resource. No human action or full traversal is needed yet.
next_action: Trace the parent routine 016866EC..01686993 and its owning/context structures, compare both local descriptor construction paths with the direct 00637660 callers, then inspect constructor paths feeding the exact root AddResource entry. If static object identity remains impossible, prepare a minimal read-only runtime capture at 00637C40/00637660 or 006388A0.
